ledger.x: 42 BC: Sicily passes from the Republic's control to Sextus; the mirror of roman-republic's loss.
42 BC: the Sicilian war opens; the Republic's own dossier carries the same contest.

40 BC: 'He captured Sardinia in 40 BC for Sextus, driving out Octavian's governor Marcus Lurius'; the Sextus Pompey page: 'in 40 BC Sextus' admiral, the freedman Menas, seized Sardinia from Octavian's governor Marcus Lurius'.
40 BC: the contest over the islands begins with the seizure.
38 BC: 'In 38 BC Menas surrendered Sardinia to Octavian and received equestrian rank as a reward.'
38 BC: the islands are Octavian's again.

September 36 BC: 'In the Battle of Naulochus, Agrippa destroyed the remainder of Sextus' fleet' (Mylae in August 36 and 'again a month later'); Lepidus and Statilius Taurus invaded Sicily and Sextus lost his base; he 'was finally captured in 35 BC, and executed without trial in Miletus'.
September 36 BC: the contest ends with Naulochus.
September 36 BC: the faction state ends with the loss of Sicily; Sextus flees to Asia Minor and dies in 35.

wars.name: Sicilian War against Sextus Pompey
wars.outcome: Pact of Misenum 39 ('Pompey was given legitimate control over Sicily and Sardinia in exchange for keeping the grain supply to Rome open'); the war resumed ('Octavian was defeated in the naval battle of Messina (37 BC)'); Naulochus 36; Sextus executed 35.

certainty.note: A faction's island territory: Sicily and, 40-38, Sardinia and Corsica; no border is drawn on any page.
